title: Partners HealthCare System / Brigham and Women's Hospital: company profile

sections.html:
Data only: this page has no written analysis. Every number below is computed from the ledger's data tables and carries a source and a retrieval date in the figures file. Tables retrieved 2026-10-12.

This ledger starts in fiscal 2010 (July 2009), the first year Massachusetts put its spending records online. Penalties, donations and lobbying before then are left out so every comparison covers the same years.

sections.heading: What the records show
sections.html:
• Penalties: the ledger holds 1 government penalty record(s) in the window, $10,000,000 in total, $10,000,000 counted. [penalties:rel:usao-ma-2017-partners-brigham:1]
  • Payments from the state and its authorities: $1.84B ($1,836,061,677) recorded as paid to this company as a vendor, fiscal 2010 to date. [contracts: company_id=partners-healthcare-brigham-and-womens; 150 rows]
  • Donations matched to the company as employer, state (OCPF): $279,639 in 1,102 gifts from 583 donors. [donations-matched: company_id=partners-healthcare-brigham-and-womens; source=OCPF; counted; 1102 rows]
  • Donations matched to the company as employer, federal (FEC): $312,887 in 610 gifts from 267 donors. [donations-matched: company_id=partners-healthcare-brigham-and-womens; source=FEC; counted; 610 rows]
  • Lobbying disclosures, 2010 onward: $6,628,948 in firm fees and in-house costs. [lobbying: company_id=partners-healthcare-brigham-and-womens; confirmed; 54 rows]
  • Statements of Financial Interest: 52 confirmed disclosure row(s) from 21 official(s) listing the company. [holdings: company_id=partners-healthcare-brigham-and-womens; confirmed; 52 rows]

State and federal donation totals are never added together. Donations are gifts by individuals who report the company as employer; they are not company money. Appearing in several of these records is an overlap in the records, not evidence that one led to another.

sections.heading: Penalties
sections.html:
How penalty amounts are counted: each row counts the cash the defendant actually paid (penalties, restitution, damages, fees). Press-release headline figures are often larger because they include debt relief, forgiven debt or rent, bill credits, conditional amounts, or proposed penalties that can still be contested. Those parts are not counted here. Every one is listed under Amounts not counted, with the headline figure, what we counted, the reason and the source. Where a release does not state the split between cash and relief, the case is left out of the totals and listed there.

How duplicates are counted: when two records describe the same payment, it is counted once. A record is left out only when a primary document read for this ledger shows the dollars are the same. When that document cannot be read, a strong match is still counted once and is marked 'possible duplicate, counted once until verified'. Records for different payments are all counted, even when the amounts are equal. Every record left out stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted, with the document behind the call.

How shared totals are counted: when several defendants pay one total, each company counts only the share its primary document states. If the document gives a total and no split, and the payers include anyone outside the one company (another company, or individuals such as owners), the total is counted for no company: it stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted. Where every payer named belongs to the one company, the whole total counts once, in full, for that company.

No amount in this company's penalty records is left out under these rules.

The penalty records, one per line:

sections.heading: Limits
sections.html:
• The window starts in fiscal 2010 (July 2009). Older records are not in this file.
  • Donors are matched to the company by the employer they report. Donors who left the field blank or wrote self-employed are missed, so the counted donations are a floor for what the matching can see.
  • Probable matches are excluded from every total: 27 OCPF and 23 FEC row(s) for this company. Held matches (reviewed and undecided) are not counted. 11 OCPF and 22 FEC confirmed rows are left out as in-kind, memo entries or pass-throughs.
  • Named individuals are not linked on profile pages.
  • Lobbying firm fees in the table start in 2010. In-house lobbying costs (the company's own staff lobbyists) are entered only from 2025, so for earlier years the lobbying figure is firm fees only. Statements of Financial Interest cover 2019 to 2025.
  • Newest period in the tables: penalties 2017-04-27; state donations 2026-09-30; federal donations 2026-08-12; lobbying 2019; holdings 2025; contracts fiscal 2027. A penalty announced after the table date is not in the ledger.
  • Totals are nominal dollars.

excluded_amounts.rule: How penalty amounts are counted: each row counts the cash the defendant actually paid (penalties, restitution, damages, fees). Press-release headline figures are often larger because they include debt relief, forgiven debt or rent, bill credits, conditional amounts, or proposed penalties that can still be contested. Those parts are not counted here. Every one is listed under Amounts not counted, with the headline figure, what we counted, the reason and the source. Where a release does not state the split between cash and relief, the case is left out of the totals and listed there.
excluded_amounts.duplicate_rule: How duplicates are counted: when two records describe the same payment, it is counted once. A record is left out only when a primary document read for this ledger shows the dollars are the same. When that document cannot be read, a strong match is still counted once and is marked 'possible duplicate, counted once until verified'. Records for different payments are all counted, even when the amounts are equal. Every record left out stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted, with the document behind the call.
excluded_amounts.shared_total_rule: How shared totals are counted: when several defendants pay one total, each company counts only the share its primary document states. If the document gives a total and no split, and the payers include anyone outside the one company (another company, or individuals such as owners), the total is counted for no company: it stays in the gross figure and is listed under Amounts not counted. Where every payer named belongs to the one company, the whole total counts once, in full, for that company.

currency.note: Newest period is the newest in the local tables. The newest contracts fiscal year is partial. Penalties are entered as of the table retrieval date; a penalty announced later is not in the ledger.
